item.description: Finally, competition authorities may take unlawful personalized pricing behavior under the General Data Protection Regulation (General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)) into account when establishing an abuse of dominance under Article 102 TFEU. Beyond classic antitrust enforcement, algorithmic pricing sits at the centre of a converging web of European digital, consumer, and data protection rules. Enforcers are no longer looking only at collusion or market power; they are policing the data inputs that fuel pricing engines and the consumer-facing tactics used to display those prices.

item.title: [CONSULTATION] [Law Firm] Proposed EU Digital Fairness Act targets addictive design, 'dark patterns' and unfair personalisation | Osborne Clarke
item.description: The proposal blacklists ten "dark patterns" considered unfair in all circumstances, which the Commission would have the power to update. The list includes false availability or popularity claims; persistent messaging throughout the ordering process creating an impression of product scarcity; defaults that consumers have to reject; inferred consent to payment for additional products; price, contract duration and automatic renewal information presented less prominently than other material information; sending fake notifications to encourage consumers to re-engage with a platform or site; and making it difficult for consumers to refuse, withdraw or change a choice they have made.
